title: Ops Runway: weekly handoff & sprint pulse (2026-08-03)
content:
Attendees: Asha (owner), Miguel, Priya, Liam, Ruth, + floating oncall (Sam)

TL;DR:
- Quiet week for customer-impacting incidents. Small flurry of quota throttles for a mid-market tenant on Friday; root cause looks like a routing misclassification combined with an aggressive token microburst.
- Control plane rollout v0.29 went to canary; noticed higher-than-expected requeue on low-priority routes. Rolling back the specific backoff change for now.
- Auth token propagation fix merged to staging, needs one more e2e run before we promote.
- Batching latency regression on one Dedicated pool remains unresolved; suspected NVLink saturation on hosts with mixed A100/RTX allocation.

Highlights / wins:
- Miguel finished the extended quota diagnostic that surfaces per-route burstiness (dashboard + alert). Initial signals helped identify the tenant above within 12 minutes.
- Priya's canary-run checklist added new synthetic scenario (10x small requests) that caught the requeue spike before the broader rollout — good catch.
- SRE playbook updated with a quicker eviction strategy for stale KV cache entries which should reduce memory-pressure incidents.

Blockers / things we need help with:
1) Batching regression on dedicated-pool-7 (owner: Liam)
   - Symptoms: p50 token latency up ~18% for requests with seq_len<64 when concurrency > 40.
   - Hypothesis: NVLink thrashing when jobs get colocated on hosts with different GPU types; scheduler isn't honoring affinity hints strongly enough.
   - Next step: repro with the nightly load generator (Miguel + Liam) and collect nvlink + dmesg during load. Need infra help to pin a repro machine for the experiment (ask infra: @Ruth).

2) Canary control plane backoff change (owner: Asha)
   - Rollout notes: v0.29 introduced adaptive backoff to reduce repeated route calculation; canary profile shows 2.1x requeues for low-priority routes under bursty load.
   - Decision: revert the backoff tweak from canary and re-evaluate parameters in a lab environment.

3) Auth propagation intermittent 401s (owner: Priya)
   - Status: fix merged (PR: linked), staging e2e failed once due to test flakiness. Need one clean run on staging + canary before prod promote.
   - Action: Priya to run 3 consecutive green e2e runs by Tue 2026-08-05 and file a stability note.

Detailed notes by topic:

Control plane (routing & route calc):
- Observed: route calc queue depth spikes correlated with a handful of low-priority clients doing short bursts. Queue backpressure triggers requeues which amplify the client-side retries.
- Temporary mitigation: increased small-req queue cap on canary; this reduced immediate requeue but surfaced the backoff regression above.
- Long-term: working hypothesis to add a short-term token bucket per-client (30s window) to cap microbursts. Design doc draft in progress (link in jira PLAT-3301).
- TODO: Asha to finish design draft and get it into arch review by 2026-08-10.

Routing (smart routing & fallbacks):
- Experiment: routing-cost heuristic change (weighting for quantized vs fp16) was sampled at 5% traffic for 48h. Observed slight cost improvements, no quality regressions.
- Note: fallback metrics need an extra label for "fallback_origin" to differentiate region vs model-variant fallbacks — Miguel to open a metric-card PR.
- Action: move experiment to 15% if no major signals by next week.

Auth (tokens, propagation, KMS):
- Root cause analysis for 401s points to a rare window where proxied requests lost temporary session headers during a short gateway restart.
- Fix implemented: re-sequencing of header flush logic to make auth fibers resilient. PR merged to staging (linked).
- Outstanding: validate compatibility with vpc-proxy (private deployments) — Priya to coordinate with Private infra team.

Quotas & throttling:
- New quota diagnostic dashboard (deployed) now shows per-route 1m/5m/15m burst ratios. This immediately helped identify the tenant that triggered the Friday throttles.
- Observed behaviour: tenant had steady background traffic + scheduled short-burst jobs (cron-based) that aligned and pushed them over temporary burst threshold.
- Action: add recommended quota profile for "cron-burst" type customers (default: tighter burst window + larger sustained allowance). Miguel to draft recommendation.

Oncall notes / recent pagers:
- Pager: quota-throttle alerts for tenant: ACME-Corp, Friday 17:42 PST.
  - Handler: Sam (oncall) followed playbook, escalated to Miguel, throttle cleared after temporary override and tenant-side dial-down.
  - Postmortem: small internal blameless note to file (owner: Miguel) by Friday 2026-08-06.

Action items (owner — due):
- Liam: repro batching regression with detailed nvlink traces; pin repro host request to infra (Ruth). Due: 2026-08-06.
- Priya: run 3 clean staging e2e runs for auth propagation fix; coordinate with Private infra for compatibility check. Due: 2026-08-05.
- Asha: rollback backoff tweak in canary and open a parameters experiment in lab; write short note for arch. Due: 2026-08-04.
- Miguel: metric-card PR to add fallback_origin label + draft quota profile for cron-burst. Due: 2026-08-10.
- Ruth: carve out 2 reproducible infra hosts for nvlink repro (one mixed A100/RTX, one homogeneous). Due: 2026-08-05.
- Sam: draft the short postmortem blameless note for ACME-Corp throttle. Due: 2026-08-06.

Notes-to-self / loose threads:
- We still need a tidy way to mark "soft-fallbacks" in traces so we can filter alert noise (low severity, expected fallbacks). Add to backlog.
- Consider a short-lived feature that exposes per-tenant microburst patterns in the Console (opt-in) — product/solutions sync needed.
- Double-check that the KV eviction change doesn't regress cold-start latency for tiny requests (Priya + SRE to add a microbenchmark).

Meeting cadence / asks for next week:
- Quick sync Mon 15min (standup) to confirm canary rollback and staging e2e results.
- Deep dive Wed 45min on batching repro results and scheduling affinity options (Liam + infra + Miguel).
- Follow-up Fri 30min for quota profile draft review (Miguel + product).

Related links / snippets:
- PLAT-3124 (quota diagnostic dashboard): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PLAT-3124
- PLAT-3301 (route calc token-bucket design): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PLAT-3301
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/889
- Slack thread: #platform-ops (8/2/26) — thread started by @sam: "quota spike ACME"

Unresolved questions:
- Is per-client token-bucket the right granularity vs per-route? (Tradeoff: state memory vs mitigation effectiveness)
- Should we preemptively pin Dedicated pools by GPU type for bursty workloads, or improve scheduler affinity heuristics?

If you see anything I missed, add to this doc and tag in the thread. We'll convert higher-confidence plans to a Confluence page once design decisions land.
